events.title: The death of St. Columba of Iona
events.shortBlurb: The Irish monk who planted the faith among the Picts from his island monastery of Iona died among his brethren…
body: Columba (Colum Cille), born in Ireland about 521 of royal Uí Néill blood, founded monasteries in his native land before crossing to Britain about 563 and establishing on the island of Iona the monastery that became the mother-house of Celtic Christianity in Scotland. From there he and his monks evangelized the Picts and trained a host of missionaries.

He died on Iona on 9 June 597, and his foundation carried the Gospel through northern Britain for generations, giving rise to such apostles as St. Aidan of Lindisfarne. He is honored as one of the great missionary saints of the Celtic Church.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 9 June
